Chapter Eight. Guarding Against Envy and Sabotage.
When you gain power or influence, you'll notice something interesting—attention follows you. And not all of it is good.
Envy is a quiet force, lurking in the background, that can chip away at even the strongest reputation or alliances. The trick? You’ve got to spot envy—not just in people around you, but also in yourself—and learn how to handle it before it grows out of control.
The first thing to remember is humility, especially when you’re riding high. If you go around flaunting your wins, showing off your perks, or making your success obvious, well, it’s almost like inviting resentment—especially from your peers or folks who work for you. But if you share credit, show gratitude, and keep your victories low-key, you’ll find it’s much easier to keep envy at bay and build genuine goodwill.
So, how do you really guard against envy and sabotage? Here are a few strategies you can count on:
Start by avoiding unnecessary displays of wealth or power. Sometimes, being subtle about your achievements is actually safer than being flashy.
Next, make a habit of praising others in public. When you shift the spotlight onto colleagues or team members, you lower your own risk and help everyone feel seen.
It also pays to notice who might be feeling left out or jealous. If you can spot the early signs of rivalry or discontent, you’ll have a chance to address it before it turns into a real issue.
And don’t forget: sometimes, the best way to neutralize a rival is to make them your ally. If you include potential detractors and recognize their value, you can turn them into supporters instead of enemies.
Picture this: there’s someone at work who’s always on top, always getting results. If that person brags about their accomplishments all the time, they’re just painting a target on their back for gossip or even sabotage. But if they share the credit, help others shine, and support their team’s growth, they’re much more likely to earn respect—and protection from those around them.
Of course, envy isn’t just something others feel. It can creep up inside you, too. Comparing yourself to others, worrying about what they have that you don’t—it’s a recipe for insecurity and bad choices. The best cure is to focus on your own growth and what you’re contributing, instead of chasing outside approval.
Sabotage doesn’t always show up with flashing lights, either. It can be subtle—snide remarks, missing information, or quiet resistance that slows down your progress. That’s why you need to stay alert, read the room, and use a bit of emotional intelligence to spot and address these issues before they snowball.
So, here’s the key takeaway: guarding against envy and sabotage comes down to humility, generosity, and real awareness. By managing both how others see you and how they feel around you, you’ll be able to protect what you’ve earned and keep the peace—no matter how high you climb.
